screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of an intervention given immediately prior to IUD insertion to reduce insertion-related pain; reports patient-reported pain with insertion and other time points.
RCT of prophylactic ibuprofen versus placebo before IUD insertion; directly measures pain immediately following insertion.

Randomized trial, but intervention is bladder filling/emptying to ease insertion rather than an analgesic or pain-prevention intervention; pain outcome is secondary and the study is primarily about insertion ease, not pain prevention.
Randomized clinical trial evaluating intracervical anesthesia before LNG-IUS insertion with pain assessed immediately and at 2 and 6 hours postprocedure, matching the review question closely.
Placebo-controlled RCT of ibuprofen prophylaxis before LNG-IUS insertion; reports pain at tenaculum placement and insertion.
Double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial of misoprostol before IUD insertion; includes pain during insertion as a secondary outcome.
Randomized placebo-controlled trial of prophylactic misoprostol prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women; patient-reported pain at multiple insertion time points was measured.

Randomized placebo-controlled trial of misoprostol before repeat LNG-IUS insertion; includes reported pain at insertion, so it fits the pain-prevention focus even though ease of insertion was primary.
Large randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of prophylactic ibuprofen before first-time IUD insertion; directly measures post-insertion pain.
Randomized controlled trial of misoprostol versus control before IUD insertion; pain during insertion is among the outcomes.
Double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial of prophylactic ibuprofen around IUD insertion; pain was assessed during insertion and after insertion up to three days.
Randomized double-blind clinical trial comparing active analgesics and placebo for pain during IUD insertion.
Randomized placebo-controlled trial of misoprostol prior to IUD insertion with patient-reported pain before and after insertion.
Randomized blinded trial of intracervical lidocaine gel versus placebo before IUD insertion; directly evaluates insertion pain.
Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled pilot study of nitroglycerin before IUD placement; reports patient-reported procedural pain.
Randomized trial comparing paracervical block with no anesthetic before IUD insertion; pain measured at tenaculum placement, insertion, and afterward.
Randomized controlled trial of lidocaine gel versus lubricant/no intervention for pain during copper IUD insertion.
Randomized placebo-controlled pilot study of intrauterine lidocaine versus saline before IUD insertion; includes pain at tenaculum placement and during insertion.
Randomized trial of misoprostol versus control before IUD insertion; pain at insertion and side effects were recorded.
Randomized double-blind clinical trial of misoprostol versus placebo before IUD insertion; reports reduction in pain during the procedure.
Randomized comparison of lavender inhalation versus placebo before IUD insertion; pain was measured immediately after insertion.
Randomized placebo-controlled trial of self-administered misoprostol before IUD insertion; pain during insertion and before discharge were assessed.
Includes a randomized placebo-controlled efficacy trial of lidocaine for IUD insertion pain, with patient-reported pain outcomes shortly after insertion.

Controlled study comparing paracervical block, placebo, and no treatment with pain scores during tenaculum placement, insertion, and after the procedure. Although not clearly described as fully randomized in the abstract, it is an intervention study on insertion-related pain and is appropriate to include conservatively.
Clinical trial randomizing nulliparous women to misoprostol or placebo before IUD insertion; primary outcome was pain at insertion.
Randomized placebo-controlled trial of vaginal lidocaine gel before IUD insertion; pain at tenaculum placement and insertion were measured, directly matching the review outcomes.
Descriptive method article and practice recommendation, not a randomized controlled trial of an intervention.
Prospective cohort study comparing history of vaginal delivery, not an intervention trial.
Qualitative interview study, not an RCT of an insertion-pain intervention.
Consensus/practice review, not primary randomized trial evidence.
Methods paper about grading evidence; no study of IUD insertion pain intervention.
Committee opinion/guideline, not an RCT.
Review article summarizing studies, not an individual randomized trial.
General review article; not a trial of IUD insertion pain prevention.
Study of pain response during a specific insertion technique without randomized intervention comparison; not an RCT of a preventive intervention.
Methodology article with no candidate intervention study.
Nonrandomized predictive cohort study; evaluates predictors of pain rather than an intervention to prevent pain.
Review/practice article, not a randomized trial.
Systematic review of multiple procedures; not an individual RCT.
Observational questionnaire study about women who chose analgesia; not randomized and not a controlled intervention trial.
General clinical report/review; not an intervention trial.
Meta-analysis of trials, not a primary randomized study.
RCT in surgical termination of pregnancy, not intrauterine contraceptive insertion.
Questionnaire/consensus-style practice article, not an RCT.
Methods/protocol paper about a collaborative meta-analysis, not a completed intervention trial.
Narrative review/commentary; not a randomized trial.
Post-insertion treatment of pain rather than prevention of insertion-related pain; the review focuses on prophylactic interventions around insertion.

Clinical trial with random allocation to lavender, placebo, and control groups, and pain after IUD insertion as the outcome. Although the abstract does not explicitly state double-blinding, it is an intervention study on insertion pain and is reasonable to include conservatively.
Technique description without clear randomized comparison; not a qualifying RCT of a preventive intervention.
Review article summarizing RCTs for pain/bleeding associated with IUD use; not a primary randomized study of insertion pain prevention.
